name: TypeScript Framework | Nutin
tagline: Designed and built a minimal frontend framework to explore explicit architecture trade-offs.
popTagline: A small frontend framework for building small, maintainable single-page applications without relying on a full framework.
popOverview: What started as an exploration of SPA architecture grew into a framework shaped by real-world use and engineering decisions. It provides just the essentials (routing, event handling, view rendering and a few quality-of-life utilities) while staying close to the DOM and standard web APIs.

sectionKeyPoints.SPA foundation: Routing, event bus and DOM-based views, with no runtime dependencies.

sectionKeyPoints.Built-in extras: i18n support, pipes and guards, and an HTTP client.

sectionKeyPoints.Tooling: A custom build pipeline, generators and a lightweight test runner.

sectionKeyPoints.Event-driven core: Navigation, view updates and cross-module communication are driven by explicit events rather than implicit state coupling.

sectionKeyPoints.Router as a coordinator: The router only matches routes and triggers view rendering; it owns no application state or business logic.

sectionKeyPoints.DOM-based views: Views render directly to the DOM, without a virtual DOM, keeping performance obvious and debugging straightforward.

sectionKeyPoints.Preventing tight coupling: As features grew, event contracts were formalized and module responsibilities kept narrow.

sectionKeyPoints.Avoiding premature generalization: Development was constrained to real needs from actual projects, keeping the codebase small and focused.

sectionKeyPoints.Testing without a framework: Lightweight test utilities built on jsdom and Node.js, favoring clarity over exhaustive automation.
